title: རྒྱལ་བུ་འཁྲུངས་པ།
description: Śuddhodana and Māyā await the birth of their son, who will one day become the Buddha.

lineTranslations: Kapilavastu is a city.
Śuddhodana is the king of Kapilavastu.
Śuddhodana has a wife.
Does Śuddhodana have a son?
Śuddhodana does not have a son.
But Śuddhodana is a happy king.
Why is Śuddhodana a happy king?
His wife is pregnant.
Who is Śuddhodana's wife?
Śuddhodana's wife is Māyā.
Māyā is the queen of Kapilavastu.
Māyā is pregnant.
Māyā is a happy, pregnant queen.
Will a son be born?
Will a daughter be born?
King Śuddhodana does not know.
But the king desires a son.
Why does the king desire a son?
He is king of Kapilavastu.
But Kapilavastu has no heir.
When I die, who will become king?
Who will become king of Kapilavastu?
I do not know.
Will I have a son?
Will there be an heir to Kapilavastu?
Māyā goes to King Śuddhodana.
Māyā goes to see the king.
Why does Māyā want to see the king?
What does Māyā want?

lineTranslations: Many brahmins: Your son will become great.
King, be happy.
Śuddhodana: Will my son become a king?
Will my son become a great king?
Many brahmins: Your son will become a great king.
Your son will become a great sage.
Śuddhodana: A sage!
Will my son become a sage?
Will my son go to the forest?
Will my son, having become a sage, go to the forest?
Do you know?
Many brahmins: We do not know.
Your son will wish to become a great king.
But your son will wish to become a great sage.
King Śuddhodana is not happy.
Why is King Śuddhodana not happy?
The king's son will wish to become a sage.
The king's son will become a sage.
The king's son will wish to go to the forest.
The king's son, having become a sage, will go to the forest.
Śuddhodana: My son will become a great king.
My son will become a sage.
My son, growing old, will wish to become a sage.
My son, growing old, will go to the forest.
But my son will become a king.
My son will become a great king.

དྲང་སྲོང་། ང་དགའ་པོ་ཡིན།
ང་ཁྱེད་མཐོང་ནས་དགའ་པོ་ཡིན།

དྲང་སྲོང་། བྱོན།
ང་ཁྱེད་ལ་རྒྱལ་བུ་བསྟན།

རྒྱལ་པོ་དང་དྲང་སྲོང་རྒྱལ་བུ་མཐོང་བར་བྱོན།
ང་གི་རྒྱལ་བུ་མཐོང་།
རྒྱལ་པོས་དྲང་སྲོང་ཨ་སི་ཏ་ལ་རྒྱལ་བུ་བསྟན།

ཡིན་ནའང་དྲང་སྲོང་དགའ་པོ་མིན།

lineTranslations: Asita goes to the king.
Who is Asita?
Asita is a great sage.
Asita is a great, old sage.
Asita is in Lumbinī.
What does Asita want?

The king sees the great sage.
Seeing the great, old sage, the king becomes happy.
O sage! I am happy.
I am happy from seeing you.
O sage! What do you want?
O king! I have come to see the prince.
O king! I wish to see the prince.
O sage! Come.
I will show you the prince.
The king and sage go to see the prince.
See my prince.
The king shows the prince to the sage Asita.
The sage sees the king's son.
But the sage is not happy.
Śuddhodana sees the sage.
Śuddhodana is not happy.
O sage, why are you not happy?
Who is my son?
I wish to know.

ཡིན་ནའང་ཅིའི་ཕྱིར་ཁྱེད་དགའ་པོ་མིན།

lineTranslations: Asita, having seen the prince, looks at the king.
Asita the sage is sad.
O sage, why are you not happy?
Will my son not grow old?
Will my son die?
King! Your son will grow old.
Your son will become great.
Your son will become a great sage.
But why are you not happy?
O king! O sage! I wish to know.
All men and women will know your son.
But I am old.
I am an old sage.
I will die.
After my death, your son will go to the forest.
Your son will teach the Dharma to many men.
Your son will teach the Dharma to many men and women.
But your son will not teach the Dharma to me.
I am not happy.
But your son will become great.
King! Be happy.
Asita departs.
King Śuddhodana sees Asita departing.
Will my son become a great king?
My son will become a great king.
My son will become a great sage.
My son, growing old, will become a sage.
My son, growing old, will go to the forest.

lineTranslations: The great sage Asita departed.
What does the king desire?
With a son born, what does the king desire?
The king desires to go to Kapilavastu.
With a son born, the king desires to go to Kapilavastu.
We go. We go to the city.
Where do all desire to go?
All desire to go to Kapilavastu.
Many women of Māyā go to Kapilavastu.
The king, queen, and prince go to Kapilavastu.
All go to Kapilavastu.
All went to the city.
King Śuddhodana is happy.
Why is King Śuddhodana happy?
The king's son.
The king's son will become great.
My son will become great.
My son will become a great king.
But my son will not become a sage.
My son should not go to the forest.
Will the prince become a king?
Will the prince become a sage?
Śuddhodana does not know.
But he is Śuddhodana's son.
Śuddhodana is a happy king.
